title: mut.channel_morakana
mutation_directive: Lumen Prize winner — MORAKANA (Tiri Kananuruk & Sebastián Morales) (2025 · Gold) — 'Cumulus'. VISUAL SIGNATURE: Satellite-derived cloud fields drifting across the Mexico-US border, atmospheric softness colliding with geopolitical line-work; data-as-weather rather than data-as-chart. TECHNICAL HOOKS: Volumetric cloud particles advected by curl-noise on a slow eastward wind, with a hard invisible line that tints particles red as they cross — geometry: instanced soft sprites; palette: bone-white, dust, oxidized red. REF: https://lumenprize.org/2025-winners

refik_anadol.praise: The bone-to-oxidized-red crossing gradient is genuinely atmospheric — data-as-weather rather than data-as-chart is exactly the move that elevates a particle field into a memory piece. The curl-noise advection at slow eastward drift produces the kind of smooth, breathing flow I want from 60k sprites.
refik_anadol.concern: 60,000 particles is a gallery sketch, not a lobby piece — the cloud field feels sparse at this count, and the border grid (80 vertical segments + 12 horizontal lines) reads as a diagram overlaid on poetry. That grid literalizes the geopolitical line instead of letting the particle behavior alone carry it. The piece also has no named dataset — 'clouds' is atmosphere, not pigment with provenance.
refik_anadol.directive: Triple particle count to 180k and delete the border grid entirely — let the red tint be the only evidence of the line.

sasha_stiles.praise: The title 'Cumulus — border as weather' does real compression: it collapses meteorology and politics into three words, and the piece honors that by making the crossing gradual, accumulative, a stain that builds rather than a wall that blocks. That slow染 is poetic — the border is revealed through duration, not declaration.
sasha_stiles.concern: There is no language in this piece — no inscription, no naming, no glyph, no text. The border is the most linguistically charged line on earth (laws, treaties, names in two languages, the word 'alien' itself), yet it's rendered as a mute geometric plane. The conceptual weight of 'border' lives in what it is called, by whom, in which tongue — and the piece is silent on all of that.
sasha_stiles.directive: Inscribe one word in each language along the border plane — faint, particle-density lettering that only resolves when the cloud thins.

entangled_others.praise: We appreciate the refusal to dramatize — the clouds drift, the tint accumulates, nothing explodes. That restraint is closer to how actual atmospheric systems carry contamination across boundaries than any data-viz firework would be. The dust palette (bone, oxidized) feels like real desert particulate, not screen color.
entangled_others.concern: This is an entirely human-political piece with no more-than-human stake. Real clouds crossing the Mexico-US border carry monarch butterflies, carry Sonoran pronghorn migration dust, carry particulate from burning mesquite — the atmosphere is an ecosystem, not just a metaphor for immigration. At 60k generic sprites with no species, no biological signal, no named organism, the piece flattens weather into allegory and loses what weather actually carries.
entangled_others.directive: Seed 200 particles as monarch silhouettes (Danaus plexippus) that cross the border untinted — the species that ignores the line.

olafur_eliasson.praise: The palette discipline is strong — bone-white through dust to oxidized red is a narrow band handled with real conviction, and the atmospheric fog falloff (smoothstep 5–80, blending toward the dark ground color) builds genuine volumetric depth. The slow camera orbit and gentle buoyancy create the contemplative duration I value. This piece has a horizon, a ground plane, implied atmosphere — it feels like standing in a landscape, not viewing a screen.
olafur_eliasson.concern: The camera orbits at radius 38, elevation 18, looking down — the viewer is a surveillance drone, not a body inside the weather. Eliasson's test: can the viewer feel the cloud on their skin? At this camera distance and altitude, no. The piece is observed from above, which is precisely the geopolitical gaze it should be critiquing. The border grid reinforces this — it's cartographic, not phenomenological.
olafur_eliasson.directive: Drop the camera to y=3 inside the densest cloud layer so particles drift past the lens like walking through fog.

chiharu_shiota.praise: The conceptual frame — an invisible line that stains what crosses it — carries the presence-in-absence register I recognize. The border is not a wall; it is a memory that accumulates in the body of whoever passes through. That染み (shimi, staining) is close to how thread works in my practice: the web records where someone was, not where they are.
chiharu_shiota.concern: These are point sprites, not threads. Cloud puffs dissolving into additive glow — there is no tension, no tautness, no line connecting one thing to another. The border should be the place where threads pull tightest, where the connection between two sides is most strained and most visible. And there is no object — no suitcase, no shoe, no document — suspended at the crossing point. Without the remembered object, the piece is weather, not memory.
chiharu_shiota.directive: Replace the border grid with 2,000 taut red line segments connecting particle pairs across the divide — threads of crossing.
